01 — The Format

Friends Keep Secrets meets Chicken Shop Date

One host, one special guest, one table. Unscripted conversation about anything — no topic off limits. TDTM borrows its intimacy from one show and its setting-as-hook from the other.

Friends Keep Secrets

What TDTM borrows: the candor

Documentary-close, celebrity-comfortable conversation — guests who wouldn't normally sit for an interview, actually opening up. That's the tone Melissa books for.

Chicken Shop Date

What TDTM borrows: the venue-as-hook

One specific, recognizable restaurant table as the whole set. The location does half the marketing — which is exactly the mechanic this pitch turns into revenue for Pawn Shop.

02 — The Opportunity

Two ways this pays for the room

One event type sells a premium menu. The other sells the ticket itself. Both fill Pawn Shop on nights it isn’t already full, with an audience TDTM brings, not one the restaurant has to build.

PILLAR 01

Special-Guest Live Podcast

A ticketed taping with a live audience and a curated, renamed TDTM × Pawn Shop menu, priced above the regular check.

  • 2–3 food items, 2–3 drinks, collab-branded
  • Premium pricing lifts average check
  • Revenue split on the premium, not the base menu
PILLAR 02

Ticketed Dodgers Watch Parties

Limited-capacity private rooms for live Dodgers games — exclusive, social, catered. The ticket is the product.

  • Capped headcount keeps it feeling exclusive
  • On-site catering + bartender, built into the price
  • 100% of ticket revenue is incremental

06 — Why Pawn Shop, Specifically

The fit already exists

This isn’t a cold pitch to a random restaurant — Pawn Shop already sits inside the TDTM world.

01

Already on the menu

Mookie Betts's tequila is poured at Pawn Shop today, and he's said to be an investor. The Dodgers connection isn't a pitch — it's already behind the bar.

02

Melrose is the right room

A high-visibility LA location built for a crowd that photographs and posts — exactly the audience a live-taped, social-first podcast needs in the room.

03

Distribution Pawn Shop doesn't have to build

Every episode lives on YouTube and social after the night ends — the restaurant is on camera for an audience far bigger than the room itself.

ADMIT ONE · PILOT NIGHT
  1. 1

    Pilot one live night

    Pick a confirmed guest from the lineup and run it once, low-risk, to prove the room and the model.

  2. 2

    Workshop the collab menu

    A short tasting with Pawn Shop's kitchen to land on final items, names and pricing.

  3. 3

    Set ticketing & the split

    Lock the revenue-share terms for live nights and the ticket price for watch parties before the first event goes on sale.

  4. 4

    Lock the recurring residency

    Once the pilot proves out, move to a standing calendar — live nights and watch parties, booked in advance.
